title: Walk Through the Gold Mine

concept.title: Move column by column: the best value of a cell comes from three cells in the previous column
body: A gold mine is a table; the number in a cell is the amount of gold there. A miner may **start at any cell of the first column**. From a cell `(i, j)` the miner moves to the next column: to `(i - 1, j + 1)`, `(i, j + 1)` or `(i + 1, j + 1)` (staying inside the table). The miner collects the gold of every cell visited. What is the **largest** amount of gold that can be collected on a walk to the last column?

Let `best(i, j)` be the largest amount collected by a walk that **ends** in the cell `(i, j)`. In the first column it is the gold of the cell itself. A walk to `(i, j)` came from one of the three cells in the previous column that can step to it, so **`best(i, j) = gold(i, j) + max of best(i - 1, j - 1), best(i, j - 1), best(i + 1, j - 1)`** (the cells that exist). The answer is the largest value in the last column.

The table is processed **column by column**, because every step moves one column to the right. This is the falling-path problem turned sideways, with a maximum instead of a minimum. The time is O(h * w) and the memory O(h). Choosing the direction of the sweep to match the direction of the moves is what makes the order of the table correct.

statement: A gold mine is a table with `h` rows and `w` columns; each cell holds some gold. A miner starts in any cell of the first column and, at each step, moves to the next column: to the cell right-up, right or right-down (if it exists). The miner collects the gold of all the cells visited, including the first one. Print the largest amount of gold that can be collected on a walk that ends in the last column.
inputFormat: The first line has `h` and `w`: the number of rows and columns.
Each of the next `h` lines has `w` numbers: one row of the table.
outputFormat: Print the largest amount of gold.

examples.note: Start with the 2 in the second row, step right-down to the 6, then right to the 4: 2 + 6 + 4 = 12.

hints: Let best(i, j) be the largest amount of gold collected by a walk that ends in the cell (i, j).
The previous cell is in the previous column: one row up, the same row or one row down.
Process the table column by column; the answer is the largest value in the last column.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
gold = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(h)]

explanation: The table is processed column by column: the best value of a cell is its gold plus the largest value among the cells of the previous column that can step to it; the answer is the largest value of the last column.

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

h, w = map(int, input().split())
gold = [list(map(int, input().split())) for _ in range(h)]

best = [gold[i][0] for i in range(h)]
for j in range(1, w):
    new = [0] * h
    for i in range(h):
        top = best[i]
        if i > 0 and best[i - 1] > top:
            top = best[i - 1]
        if i + 1 < h and best[i + 1] > top:
            top = best[i + 1]
        new[i] = top + gold[i][j]
    best = new
print(max(best))
